content:
Rafael Mendes: circling back on Dedicated throughput SLO burn-rate thresholds. need to lock paging policy today for ENG-19288 + the alert config PR. what are we comfortable paging on vs ticket?

Sean Gallagher: +1. reminder: throughput SLO is a “floor” on tokens/sec per deployment_id, measured on the canonical metric (post-streaming fix). objective is to catch real customer impact, not every transient dip.

Aisha Bello: current draft uses multi-window burn rate (fast+slow). but the numbers are still placeholders. also we need to decide what qualifies as a customer-impacting incident (SEV2?) vs “watch it.”

Allison Grant: from obs side, our standard is “page only when both windows fire” to avoid flapping. we can do:
- fast: 5m window, burn_rate > X
- slow: 1h window, burn_rate > Y
…and require both.

Sergio Costa: question: what’s our error budget period here? 30d? and SLO target 99%?

Sean Gallagher: Dedicated throughput SLO is 99% compliance over rolling 30d (per deployment). i.e., 1% budget = ~7h12m per 30d.

Rafael Mendes: ok. then burn rate math is the usual: burn_rate = (1 - compliance) / (1 - objective).

Aisha Bello: for thresholds, i’m leaning to the Google SRE recommended pairs (14.4 / 6) style, but tuned so we don’t page on a single node hiccup.

Allison Grant: for a 30d window, canonical “page” pair is often:
- 5m burn_rate > 14.4 AND 1h burn_rate > 6
That means: burning the full 30d budget in ~2d (slow) / ~0.5d (fast) if sustained.

Sergio Costa: 5m/1h feels right, but do we also want a “ticket” alert for longer, low-grade erosion? like 6h/1d.

Rafael Mendes: yes, ticket is important for capacity/shape saturation trends. but we should keep it out of paging.

Sean Gallagher: propose 2 alert classes:
1) PAGE (oncall SRE): 5m > 14.4 AND 1h > 6
2) TICKET (SRE backlog / #dedicated-slo): 6h > 3 AND 1d > 1

Aisha Bello: +1, but we need to sanity check against expected variance during warmups / model rollouts. does SLO evaluator exclude “warm pool spinup” windows?

Sean Gallagher: exclusions: provisioning warmup (first 10 minutes after a new replica becomes ready) is excluded from SLO accounting. also customer throttling / client-side backpressure isn’t counted (we drop samples where admission_control says throttled_by_customer).

Keiko Yamamoto: on admission control: if we shed at the edge to protect floor, we’ll see fewer requests but throughput floor metric should still be computed on serviced tokens/sec. we should confirm we’re not inadvertently counting queued time.

Logan Wright: metric pipeline detail: throughput is computed from token emit events / wall time, tagged by deployment_id + model + region. no queue time included. we do have a “time_in_queue_ms” metric separately.

Rafael Mendes: ok, next: “when is this customer impacting?” we need a crisp rule for incident bot + comms.

Aisha Bello: suggestion:
- if PAGE alert fires for any Premium deployment => open incident (SEV2) automatically
- if PAGE alert fires for Standard/Plus => page oncall, but incident only if sustained > 15 min or confirmed by CS ticket

Sean Gallagher: small tweak: base it on actual “below floor” duration, not just burn rate. burn rate can spike w/ low traffic.

Allison Grant: agreed. burn-rate alone can be noisy if denominator is small. can we add an additional gate: “throughput_floor_ratio < 0.9” for N minutes?

Sergio Costa: we can. dashboard already has “floor adherence ratio” = observed_tokens_per_sec / committed_floor. we can alarm on that too.

Rafael Mendes: careful: we said canonical SLO is burn-rate (error budget). but for paging, adding a second condition is fine as a guard.

Sean Gallagher: proposal:
PAGE when:
(A) burn_rate_5m > 14.4 AND burn_rate_1h > 6
AND
(B) floor_adherence_p50_5m < 0.9 (or p10?)

Aisha Bello: p50 might hide partial brownout (some requests ok, tail bad). p10 is sensitive. maybe p25?

Allison Grant: we’ve used p25 in other systems as a middle ground. also define it on “active minutes” only (minutes with >= X tokens emitted) to avoid dividing by near-zero.

Logan Wright: we can filter to active minutes via a recording rule: active = tokens_emitted > 5k/min (tunable). i can add that label filter in the PromQL.

Mina Haddad: from routing side: if we’re in failover mode (tier-aware routing sends to secondary pool), throughput might be slightly lower but still within floor. if floor is violated, that’s a bigger deal since it likely means we’re saturated across pools.

Rafael Mendes: so for Premium: PAGE + open incident if condition holds for 10 min. for Plus/Standard: PAGE only (no auto incident) unless holds 30 min.

Sean Gallagher: + include a “capacity exhausted” annotation if saturation signals are high (gpu_util > 95%, queue_depth > threshold) to speed triage.

Sergio Costa: i can add those annotations to the alert template + link to the dedicated dashboard panels.

Aisha Bello: what about partial region outage? should we page if a single region’s Dedicated deployment is below floor but failover is functioning (customer still meets floor overall)?

Sean Gallagher: SLO is per deployment_id and deployment is region-scoped for Dedicated. if region fails and we fail over cross-region, that’s a different product posture (Premium may have it). for now, we page on per-deployment SLO regardless; the incident severity can reflect whether customer is seeing degraded latency/throughput.

Rafael Mendes: ok, finalizing:
- Error budget: 30d rolling, objective 99%
- PAGE: burn_rate_5m>14.4 AND burn_rate_1h>6 AND floor_adherence_p25_5m<0.9 on active minutes
- TICKET: burn_rate_6h>3 AND burn_rate_1d>1 (no extra gate)
- Auto-incident:
  * Premium: if PAGE persists 10 min => open SEV2 + notify #customer-success
  * Plus/Standard: if PAGE persists 30 min => open SEV3; otherwise oncall triage only
Sound right?

Allison Grant: works for me. please add a note that these are “pre-GA thresholds” and we’ll tune after the alert-noise review.

Aisha Bello: ack. i’ll update the PR (pr-19405) with the thresholds + p25 gate + active-minutes filter. also will add runbook links.

Sergio Costa: i’ll update dashboard panels to show the same p25 floor adherence + active flag so people can reconcile alert vs graph.

Logan Wright: i’ll sanity check the active-minutes recording rule doesn’t drop legitimate low-traffic customers (esp. embeddings-heavy). might need a per-route threshold.

Sean Gallagher: + please ensure we’re on the post-streaming double-count fix version (pr-19422). otherwise burn rate will be nonsense for streaming.

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: locking this unless objections by EOD. i’ll post summary to #announcements + tag Lauren so Product is aligned on incident policy.
